summary: Santa Maria is a tight, puzzly engine-builder where you tetris polyomino buildings onto your colony board and use dice as workers that trigger entire rows/columns before getting stuck in place. Turns are quick but the spatial planning is dense, rewarding careful sequencing of dice placement and building layout over three tense rounds.
praised: Clever dice-as-workers mechanic where placement order and position matter enormously
Satisfying polyomino/tetris-like puzzle of fitting buildings onto your board
Fast turns and low downtime despite the depth
High replayability from varied building tiles and monk/scholar choices
criticised: Steep learning curve and fiddly rules explanation for newcomers
Can feel overwhelming or 'mathy'/optimization-heavy rather than thematic
Iconography and symbol-heavy components require a learning period
Thin theme pasted onto an abstract engine-building puzzle
Only three rounds means early mistakes are hard to recover from

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting competition for dice and buildings

scoring.why: Happiness points accumulate from building layout efficiency, shipping routes, conquistadors, and monk types, so the winner is whoever builds the most efficient multi-source engine.
